The bug was that `Dataset.set_xindex` silently ignored any extra variables returned by `Index.create_variables()`. I have modified `xarray/core/dataset.py` to ensure that all variables returned by `create_variables()` are added to the dataset's variables and that they are correctly recognized as coordinates by updating `coord_names` in the `_replace` call.

Specifically:
1.  Updated the `len(coord_names) == 1` branch to use `variables.update(new_coord_vars)` instead of only updating the specific coordinate name.
2.  Updated the `else` branch (for multi-indexes) to include a loop that adds any variables from `new_coord_vars` that are not part of `coord_names`.
3.  Updated the final `_replace` call to include `set(new_coord_vars.keys())` in the `coord_names` set, ensuring that any new variables created by the index are treated as coordinates.

These changes ensure that custom indexes can introduce new coordinates to the dataset during the `set_xindex` process.
